title: Route-path telemetry and per-hop decision logs for smart routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Provide structured, queryable telemetry that explains why each inference request was routed the way it was. Deliverables: 1) Decision log record model (JSON schema) emitted for every routed request (or sampled subset) containing: routing_key, selected_region, selected_tier, selected_model_variant, candidate_alternates (with scores), decision_reasons (policy rules hit), latency_budget_ms, observed_queue_ms, observed_inference_ms, fallback_trigger (if any), and trace_id. 2) Per-hop timing spans for routing pipeline (ingress -> policy-eval -> placement -> enqueue -> serve -> postprocess), exported to existing OpenTelemetry collector. 3) Per-route metrics: p50/p95 routing-decision-latency, fallback-rate, variant-switch-rate, cross-region-forward-rate. 4) Queryable index in observability backend (logs -> ES/ClickHouse) for ad-hoc forensic queries and long-term aggregation. Requirements/constraints: - Backwards-compatible schema evolution; new fields must be optional. - Sampling policy: default 1% decision logs for low-volume accounts, 100% for P0 customers and those in Dedicated/Private. - PII/LLM-output exclusion: decision logs must never record model outputs or full prompts; only hashed prompt prefix metadata and prompt length. - Storage retention: decision logs retained 90 days by default; per-customer overrides for enterprise. - Cost control: batch events and compress before shipping; allow customers to opt-out of decision logging. Integration points: - Routing service (routing-service) instrumentation: emit log and create span. - Placement/pool manager: include pool selection metadata. - Runtime fallback layer: emit fallback_trigger and fallback_variant. Acceptance criteria: - Schema doc published in Confluence linked below. - End-to-end test that asserts decision log appears for sampled requests and contains required fields. - Dashboard with fallback-rate and routing-decision-latency per-region. - Load test to verify no more than 5% CPU overhead on routing-service under sustained peak with 1% sampling.
comments: 2025-02-14 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket and initial spec draft. Mapped to Smart Routing Observability project. Assigned to Liam for implementation plan.

2025-02-15 - Liam O'Connor: Spike completed. Confirmed we can reuse existing OTEL spans; will add a dedicated 'routing.decision' span with attributes described. Implementation plan: add a decision-log writer with sampling hooks and a batched uploader to ClickHouse/ES.

2025-02-17 - Design review (Kavya Suresh): Reviewed schema. Request: add 'policy_version' and 'evaluation_snapshot' (short string) fields so we can trace rule changes. Also requested a redaction rule for prompt hashes.
2025-02-18 - Security (Marco Ruiz): Security review: confirmed PII exclusion acceptable. Must add KMS-tagging for enterprise-stored logs. Marking security_review_required=true.
2025-02-19 - Ops (Jing Wei): Suggested retention default 90 days and a TTL mechanism. Raised concern about ClickHouse ingest costs; proposed sampling thresholds per tenant and nightly downsampling.

2025-02-20 - Liam O'Connor: Implementing: added routing.decision span, decision_log protobuf, and uploader. Working on feature flag (ff-routing-decision-logs) to control rollout. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1132
2025-02-21 - PM (Sofia Martinez): Approved scope for cycle 2025-W07. Please add dashboard mockups before merging.
notes: Trade-offs considered: 1) Full 100% recording yields best forensic power but is cost-prohibitive; settled on sampled default + per-customer overrides. 2) Storing near-real-time decision logs in ClickHouse for fast queries vs. cheaper cold storage; decided to keep recent 90 days in fast store and archive older data. Rollout plan: - Phase 1 (canary): enable for internal tenants + 2 enterprise customers - Phase 2: enable sampling by default at 1% for public tenants - Phase 3: dashboards and alerting + opt-out controls in Console.
